calculation.preparation: Epoch's registry identifies U.S. sites; dated site states are summed as operational IT power. Independently measured MLPerf server goodput and full-system power set reference token-equivalents per IT GW-day, while a matched MLPerf series sets productivity velocity. H100-equivalents remain an audit cross-check only. Physical power, productivity, inference allocation, Personal-AI allocation, and workload are then combined into supported-user equivalents.
calculation.countdownEffect: Converts physical IT power and inference productivity into supported Personal-AI users. The gate passes only when service capacity reaches 100% of the selected population target.

update.notes: Refresh Epoch's data-center registry and timeline together, recompute every quarter from the dated U.S. site states, and refresh comparable MLPerf power submissions separately. Select an absolute latency-constrained reference result and a matched workload series for productivity velocity; do not derive productivity from H100e. Refresh independent build-rate and allocation outlooks as supporting evidence without merging global watts into the U.S. series.

inferenceProductivityObservations.comparabilityNote: Matched to the v5.1 Llama 2 70B 99.9 Server row. Reference-token equivalence multiplies measured tokens per joule by 70B/100B; the same factor cancels from the two-point growth rate.
Matched to the v5.0 Llama 2 70B 99.9 Server row. The measured reference-token productivity is 2.8181× the v5.0 point over 160 days.

The gate uses this measured latency-constrained large-model result as its absolute baseline. Reference-token equivalence multiplies measured tokens per joule by 405B/100B; no H100-equivalent field enters the calculation.
